title: Compact failover contracts for A/B traffic slices
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Introduce CompactFailoverContract DSL for per-slice failover and graceful degradation. New runtime hooks for preemptive degrade and synthetic shadow replay. Backwards compatible; opt-in via rollout spec.
description:
Motivation: Existing rollout mechanisms apply global or cohort-wide policies which are heavy-weight for tiny A/B slices and increase blast radius when failovers happen. This PR adds a compact, declarative contract that binds a traffic slice to a lightweight failover strategy (soft-hedge) and deterministic replay rules for shadow traffic. The goal is to make micro-slices (0.1% - 2% traffic) safe to run heterogeneous model variants with minimal operational overhead.

Summary of changes: Implements a CompactFailoverContract DSL, slice-resident state for fail counters and soft hedges, deterministic synthetic shadowing that replays a sampled subset of traffic to a candidate model variant, and a runtime hook to preemptively degrade to a cheaper model variant if error/failure thresholds are hit. Adds end-to-end integration tests and a runbook doc for on-call.

Checklist:
- [x] CompactFailoverContract schema and parser
- [x] Runtime recovery hooks (preemptive degrade + auto-recover)
- [x] Deterministic synthetic shadowing + replay throttle
- [x] Telemetry: per-slice SLI counters and ring buffer for recent failures
- [x] Integration tests and canary harness emulation
- [x] Docs: runbook & API examples

Design notes: The contract is intentionally compact (single line binding in rollout spec) to encourage usage on many small slices; complexity is pushed into runtime that keeps slice-local, memory-bounded state (failure ring buffer + soft-hedge counter). Failure thresholds are relative (delta to baseline) to avoid noisy absolute cutoffs. Soft-hedge is a short-duration diversion to a fallback model variant; it automatically unwinds if the slice returns to baseline. Synthetic shadowing uses a seed-based deterministic sampler so replay results are reproducible for debugging.

Compatibility: Opt-in only. No changes to existing rollout API surface unless users reference the new CompactFailoverContract object. Migration notes included in docs.

CI/QA: CI had one intermittent e2e failure on first run (integration/rollout_sim_test) tied to time-sensitive scheduling; test was flakey under 2ms system clock jitter. Test was hardened and rerun, full CI green.

Related: ENG-1423 (safety contracts), SUP-987 (customer incident that motivated per-slice failover), ENG-1488 (telemetry portability).

How to review: Focus on the runtime contract semantics in rollout/orchestrator/contract.go and the safety properties in scheduler/slice_guard.go. The core algorithm is described in-line as comments in contract.go and tests cover edge cases (slice churn, rapid spike, partial-memory eviction).

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can we bound memory usage of the ring buffer under high-slice-count scenarios? Suggest keeping N configurable with sane default. -> Priya: Yes, made size configurable via rollout.runtime.sliceRingSize with default 64 entries.

Omar Lopez: How does this interact with KV cache reuse across variants? If we degrade to a smaller variant, we might want to evict large kvs. -> Priya: Added a small eviction hint via runtime hook; eviction is best-effort and non-blocking.

Lina Svensson: Tests look good but add a smoke test for deterministic replay seed stability across restarts. -> Priya: Added integration test that simulates restart and validates seed-stable sampling.

notes_for_oncall: New per-slice metrics exported under metric key redwood.rollout.slice.failures and redwood.rollout.slice.soft_hedge. Runbook at docs/runbooks/compact_failover.md includes steps to backfill ring buffer snapshots to S3 for postmortem. Soft-hedge durations default to 30s; tuning should be done cautiously to avoid oscillation.
attention_points: Opt-in feature but telemetry rollup will show increased cardinality when used widely. Recommend gradual adoption and monitoring of cardinality before enabling fleet-wide.
